reading: Objects are sorted by colour into two columns (the colour that starts further left takes the left column at x=0, the other starts one column after the first column's width); within each colour the objects are left-aligned and stacked from the bottom row upward with one empty row between them, the object that was leftmost in the input at the bottom.
verb: sort and stack objects by colour

slots.column order: colour whose leftmost cell is further left goes to the left column
slots.column x: left column at x=0; right column at x = left column width + 1
slots.stack order: within a colour, the object with the smaller leftmost x sits at the bottom
slots.stacking: bottom-aligned to the last row, left-aligned, one blank row between objects

why: every output object is an input object of the same shape and colour, repositioned; output size equals input size

reading: The 3x3 grid of 5x5 panels is permuted: each panel moves to the panel position that matches where its marks sit inside the panel (top-left marks to the top-left panel, right-edge marks to the middle-right panel, etc.); the panel with marks all round (symmetric) goes to the centre.

slots.panels: nine 5x5 panels cut by the background separator lines
slots.key per panel: direction (row band, column band) of the panel's minority-colour cells relative to the panel centre; balanced/symmetric panel = centre
slots.placement: panel pasted at the panel slot of that direction

why: the output panels are exactly the input panels, permuted

reading: Within each region cut by the full separator lines: if the region contains a short 4-coloured divider line, the two halves on either side of it swap (reflect across the 4 line); otherwise every 1-coloured block in the region takes the colour of the region's one non-1 block.
verb: swap across divider or fill placeholders

slots.regions: areas cut by full separator lines (colour 5/7/9)
slots.case A: region holds a 4-coloured divider: reflect the blocks across the divider (swap the two sides)
slots.case B: no divider: recolour all 1-blocks to the colour of the other block in the region

why: blocks keep their 3x3 shape and position slots; only colours of blocks change

reading: The grid is a periodic lattice of 1/2 lines; a few cells are marked 8. Every other place in the lattice with the same local line context as a marked motif gets the same 8 motif (the 8 overlay is completed consistently with the lattice structure, including its transpose symmetry).
verb: copy mark motif to matching lattice spots

slots.motif: each 8-coloured component (with the original colour under it)
slots.match: translations/transposes of the lattice where the surrounding row/column line types equal those around the motif

why: only lattice cells (1 or 2) become 8; nothing else changes

reading: Each row that holds a 1 and later an 8 contributes the strip of cells strictly between them; the output stacks these strips top to bottom (all strips have the same width).

slots.rows: input rows containing both a 1 and an 8 (1 left of 8)
slots.strip: cells strictly between the 1 and the 8 on that row

why: each output row equals the between-segment of one marked input row

reading: Several plus-shaped crosses of colour 2 are partly hidden by noise; each cross is completed (both arms, same arm length for all crosses in the grid) and every missing cross cell is painted 8.

new_rows.name: plus_gap
new_rows.datalog:
two(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 2).
hn(Y, X, count(X2)) :- px(Y, X, C), two(Y, X2), D = X2 - X, E = X - X2, D < 4, E < 4.
vn(Y, X, count(Y2)) :- px(Y, X, C), two(Y2, X), D = Y2 - Y, E = Y - Y2, D < 4, E < 4.
sc(Y, X, S) :- hn(Y, X, H), vn(Y, X, V), S = H + V.
ext(Y, X, D) :- sc(Y, X, S), two(Y, X2), D = X2 - X, E = X - X2, D < 4, E < 1.
ext(Y, X, D) :- sc(Y, X, S), two(Y, X2), D = X - X2, E = X2 - X, D < 4, E < 1.
ext(Y, X, D) :- sc(Y, X, S), two(Y2, X), D = Y2 - Y, E = Y - Y2, D < 4, E < 1.
ext(Y, X, D) :- sc(Y, X, S), two(Y2, X), D = Y - Y2, E = Y2 - Y, D < 4, E < 1.
reach(Y, X, max(D)) :- ext(Y, X, D).
near(Y, X, Y2, X2) :- sc(Y, X, S), sc(Y2, X2, S2), A = Y2 - Y, B = Y - Y2, P = X2 - X, Q = X - X2, A < 4, B < 4, P < 4, Q < 4.
beaten(Y, X) :- near(Y, X, Y2, X2), sc(Y, X, S), sc(Y2, X2, S2), S2 > S.
beaten(Y, X) :- near(Y, X, Y2, X2), sc(Y, X, S), sc(Y2, X2, S), reach(Y, X, L), reach(Y2, X2, L2), L2 < L.
centre(Y, X) :- sc(Y, X, S), !beaten(Y, X).
arm(max(L)) :- centre(Y, X), reach(Y, X, L).
plus(Y, X) :- centre(Yc, X), arm(L), px(Y, X, C), D = Y - Yc, E = Yc - Y, M = L + 1, D < M, E < M.
plus(Y, X) :- centre(Y, Xc), arm(L), px(Y, X, C), D = X - Xc, E = Xc - X, M = L + 1, D < M, E < M.
plus_gap(Y, X) :- plus(Y, X), !two(Y, X).

why: every non-2 cell on a completed cross becomes 8; all other cells are unchanged

reading: Each 6-coloured shape takes the colour of the single marker cell nearest to it; the recoloured shapes are cropped to their boxes and placed side by side (or stacked, following how they are laid out in the input) to form the output.
verb: recolour by nearest marker and pack

slots.colour: colour of the nearest single-cell marker
slots.layout: cropped shapes concatenated along the axis on which they are spread in the input (left-to-right or top-to-bottom), in input order

why: each output block is one input shape's box with 6 replaced by its marker's colour

reading: An anti-diagonal segment of 2 of length n is replaced by the next segment of a staircase growing from the bottom-left corner: length n+1, starting at the diagonal cell just above-right of the old segment's top-right end (segments of lengths 1,2,3,4,... laid end to end along one anti-diagonal).

slots.subject: the single 2-coloured anti-diagonal segment (length n)
slots.new segment: anti-diagonal of length n+1 on the same line, beginning at the cell diagonally up-right of the old segment's upper end

why: output has one anti-diagonal segment, one cell longer than the input's, on the same diagonal line from the bottom-left corner

reading: The one 8-coloured shape is a template; every placement of that shape (in any of its four rotations) lying entirely on 3-cells is recoloured 8.

new_rows.name: shape_match
new_rows.datalog:
eight(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 8).
three(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 3).
ty(min(Y)) :- eight(Y, X).
tx(min(X)) :- ty(Y), eight(Y, X).
tpl(DY, DX) :- eight(Y, X), ty(Y0), tx(X0), DY = Y - Y0, DX = X - X0.
rot(0, EY, EX) :- tpl(EY, EX).
rot(1, EY, EX) :- tpl(DY, DX), EY = DX, EX = 0 - DY.
rot(2, EY, EX) :- tpl(DY, DX), EY = 0 - DY, EX = 0 - DX.
rot(3, EY, EX) :- tpl(DY, DX), EY = 0 - DX, EX = DY.
bad(Y0, X0, R) :- px(Y0, X0, C), rot(R, EY, EX), Y = Y0 + EY, X = X0 + EX, !three(Y, X).
good(Y0, X0, R) :- px(Y0, X0, C), rot(R, EY, EX), !bad(Y0, X0, R).
shape_match(Y, X) :- good(Y0, X0, R), rot(R, EY, EX), Y = Y0 + EY, X = X0 + EX.

why: every 3 cell covered by a rotated placement of the 8-template becomes 8; nothing else changes

reading: The one shape that contains an 8 cell is cut out to its 3x3 box, and the 8 is repainted with the shape's own colour.
why: output is the box of the multi-coloured component with its single 8 cell recoloured to the surrounding colour
invariants: shape form of the marked object
